intensity_columns_used: LFQ intensity 50amol_1, LFQ intensity 50amol_2, LFQ intensity 50amol_3, LFQ intensity 125amol_1, LFQ intensity 125amol_2, LFQ intensity 125amol_3, LFQ intensity 250amol_1, LFQ intensity 250amol_2, LFQ intensity 250amol_3, LFQ intensity 500amol_1, LFQ intensity 500amol_2, LFQ intensity 500amol_3, LFQ intensity 2500amol_1, LFQ intensity 2500amol_2, LFQ intensity 2500amol_3, LFQ intensity 5000amol_1, LFQ intensity 5000amol_2, LFQ intensity 5000amol_3, LFQ intensity 12500amol_1, LFQ intensity 12500amol_2, LFQ intensity 12500amol_3, LFQ intensity 25000amol_1, LFQ intensity 25000amol_2, LFQ intensity 25000amol_3, LFQ intensity 50000amol_1, LFQ intensity 50000amol_2, LFQ intensity 50000amol_3
filtering_rule: Removed rows flagged Reverse=Yes, Potential contaminant=Yes, or Only identified by site=Yes
missing_value_strategy: No imputation. Proteins detected in all 6 replicates of a contrast (3 per amount) are tested with a t-test; other proteins are handled by a one-sided presence/absence rule
normalization_method: None (constant yeast amount and controlled UPS1 spike-in; sample medians inspected as QC only)
test_method: Two-sample Welch t-test on log2 LFQ intensities (3 vs 3 replicates), BH adjustment within each contrast, FDR cutoff 0.05
presence_absence_rule: Detected in all 3 replicates of the higher amount and missing in at least one replicate of the lower -> significant up. The reverse pattern (present at lower, absent at higher) is not called: in this concentration-dependent spike-in it is an expected detection artifact, not a decrease. Mixed detection within an amount is not called.
processing_order: read -> clean (decoy/contaminant/site flags) -> QC medians and missingness -> log2 transform -> contrast-wise two-sample t-test with BH correction for fully detected proteins -> one-sided presence/absence rule for the rest
